item.title: From AWS Lambda to Cloudflare Workers: free tiers and cold starts
item.description: In the previous article I described how I fitted a Telegram volleyball organizer bot into the AWS Free Tier: Lambda + S3 + EventBridge, at about zero dollars. That setup ran for months. Then I moved the same bot to Cloudflare Workers and R2 — the same Go, the same JSON state files, the same Gemini router.

item.title: How I Deployed an AI Telegram Bot to AWS for Free
item.description: For over three years, I have been organizing volleyball games in our Telegram community. At first, we used standard Telegram polls, but the routine kept growing, so I decided to automate the process. That is how an AI-powered organizer bot was born, and the whole architecture is built around it.

item.title: Deploying Telegram Bot to AWS Lambda with Function URL
item.description: This article is a continuation of “Building an AI Telegram Bot with Go, Gemini API, and AWS Lambda” and contains detailed instructions for setting up and deploying a Telegram bot to AWS Lambda using Function URL.

item.title: Building an AI Telegram Bot with Go, Gemini API, and AWS Lambda
item.description: In this article, we’ll explore how to build an intelligent Telegram bot using Go that acts as a proxy between users and Google’s Gemini API. The bot will handle two primary functions: answering user messages and generating images. While this mechanism can be significantly extended with additional capabilities like voice and video generation, we’ll focus on these two request types for simplicity.
